loggia_thermal_consequence.finding: !! THE ЛОДЖИЯ IS THERMALLY DECOUPLED FROM THE FLAT, AND THAT CUTS AGAINST THE OWNER'S OWN GOAL.
reasoning: The wall between the flat and the лоджия - M1, plus M7 and the insulated face of R8 - is full warm perimeter: 300 mm block with 70 mm of mineral wool.
So essentially NO heat leaks from the heated flat into the лоджия. One might otherwise have assumed some did.
M2 separates this лоджия from the neighbour's, and both are unheated - cold-to-cold, no help from that side either.
The лоджия's own enclosure is thin and uninsulated by design: M2 'thinner', M6b ~200 mm provisional.
The floor and ceiling are slabs shared with the loggias above and below, which are also unheated.
loggia_thermal_consequence.consequence: !! THE STANDING TARGET - keep the лоджия frost-free through an ordinary Belarusian winter with NO heating, on passive measures alone - therefore rests on exactly two things: SOLAR GAIN, and the лоджия's OWN enclosure. Nothing is contributed by the flat.
loggia_thermal_consequence.the_good_news: Solar gain is the best it could be: the лоджия's main angled glazing faces DUE SOUTH (confirmed orientation), making it the most solar-exposed element in the flat.
loggia_thermal_consequence.the_work: So the glazing upgrade the owner is already planning is doing nearly all of the work, and the thin uninsulated enclosure walls (M2, M6b) are the weak points. Whether the target is achievable at all is an open question the vault has already flagged as a content gap - see 00_Master/Family_Requirements.md section 10 - and this is the constraint set that question has to be answered against.
loggia_thermal_consequence.note_on_scope: The owner has decided NOT to join the лоджия to the flat and to keep its doors and windows. That decision is unaffected; what changes is where the heat has to come from.

insulation_is_NOT_uniform_2026_09_04.consequence_for_heat_loss: Any heat-loss calculation must use 150 mm over R8/R9 and 70 mm over the M-series, not a single figure. The thermal-bridge treatment is already designed in, which is a point in the building favour.

three_ways_they_behave_unlike_walls: 1. IMMOVABLE - common property serving the whole riser. No layout variant may touch them.

3. They cannot be chased or drilled, unlike the aerated block around them - so no service may cross them.

junction_convention_2026_09_04.rule: !! Every wall length is the CLEAR INTERNAL run, face to face between its neighbours. No wall’s length includes any part of a wall it touches, and no two wall solids may overlap.
junction_convention_2026_09_04.owner_wording: "R1a and R1b are crossing at the corner, that shouldn’t be so - the walls cannot overlap. When we calculate the length of a wall section we should take a look at the thickness of the one it is adjacent to, because we shouldn’t double count the thickness of the walls."
junction_convention_2026_09_04.the_other_half_of_it: Nothing is double-counted, which was his point - but nothing may be silently UNDER-counted either. Corner and T-junction volumes belong to no wall under this convention, so they are carried as a separate junction allowance rather than quietly lost from the quantities.
junction_convention_2026_09_04.why_it_is_also_the_practical_choice: It matches how the flat will actually be measured in three months: a tape held inside a room reads the clear run.
junction_convention_2026_09_04.enforced_by: tools/layout/check_wall_crossings.py, over data/canonical/wall_runs.csv. Run it after any change to the geometry.
junction_convention_2026_09_04.what_the_sweep_found: !! The owner spotted R1a x R1b (147 mm overlap). Sweeping all 25 runs found a SECOND instance he had not spotted: G2 x G4C (166 mm), where G4C was drawn running through the top wall. Both fixed. That is precisely why this became a script rather than a habit - one crossing was visible and the other was not, and the difference between them was luck.
junction_convention_2026_09_04.SUPERSEDED: !! The "separate junction allowance" half of this entry was WRONG and is replaced by corner_ownership_2026_09_04. Clear-internal-everywhere cannot double-count a corner, but it leaves every L-corner unfilled - and the owner is right that a void is as wrong as an overlap. The clear-run rule itself stands; what changes is that corners are OWNED, not allowanced.

corner_ownership_2026_09_04.owner_wording: "One bad thing is overlapping. Another bad thing is creating a void. A correct junction is, for example, MA and R8, R8 and MB - a perfect corner when you take the thickness into account. If we connect R1a and R1b we get a void at the very corner. You should extend either R1b or R1a by the thickness, 250 mm. And the same 250 to either G3 or R2."
corner_ownership_2026_09_04.rule: !! Every wall carries TWO lengths. clear_mm is what the plan prints and what a tape held inside the room reads. solid_mm is clear_mm plus the thickness of every corner THAT wall owns. At each L-corner exactly one wall runs through to the other’s far face and the other stops on its near face, so the corner volume is counted once - never twice, never zero times.
corner_ownership_2026_09_04.ownership_is_deterministic: 1: the thicker wall owns the corner (the envelope beats a partition). 2: on a tie, the longer run (the continuous line beats a stub). 3: on a tie, alphabetically first, only so the output is stable.
corner_ownership_2026_09_04.why_that_rule_is_trusted: Rule 1 independently reproduces the two junctions the owner named as ALREADY CORRECT - MA over R8 and MB over R8 - without being told which walls are external. That is the test that it is the right rule rather than a convenient one.
corner_ownership_2026_09_04.the_ten_corners: MB +250 +250 = +500 (R8 and R9, at both its ends) · R1a +250 · G3 +250 · MA +250 · G4a +120 · R1b +120 · G4d +75 · R4 +75 · R5 +75. Every other wall: solid_mm = clear_mm. G3’s +250 applies to the R3+G3 pair, whose solid run is therefore 5830 + 250 = 6080 - exactly what the owner’s own top-edge chain does when it appends R2’s thickness after the 3315.
corner_ownership_2026_09_04.MY_FIRST_ATTEMPT_WAS_THE_WRONG_INSTRUMEN: !! I first wrote a resolver that snapped the drawn pixel runs until every corner closed. It moved R2 by 27 mm, G8 by 77 and G4d by 58 - figures that come from printed dimensions and the owner’s own chains - in order to satisfy a raster registration only good to ~50 mm. Deleted. The drawing LOCATES walls; the printed dimensions DEFINE them. The corner decision belongs in the lengths, not in the picture. This is the same lesson as junction_correction_2026_09_04 (blob edges locate, printed dimensions fix) arriving in a new disguise, and I did not recognise it until the diff showed his numbers moving.
corner_ownership_2026_09_04.what_the_sweep_found_beyond_what_he_name: He named R1a×R1b and G3×R2. Checking all 25 runs found 8 voids and 3 bad T-junctions, including G4C drawn CROSSING G4d and G4d ending 203 mm short of G4a’s face. All fixed.

corner_ownership_2026_09_04.RULE_CORRECTED_the_frame_owns_the_corner: !! Rule 1 was "the thicker wall owns the corner". WRONG, and the owner’s own arithmetic falsified it within the hour. The rule is THE CONCRETE FRAME OWNS THE CORNER: the developer’s description, already in building_spec.json, reads "монолитный железобетонный каркас с наружными стенами (не несущие) из блоков" - the frame is cast first and the blocks are non-load-bearing infill built against it. So a 250 concrete column owns its corner even where a 300+70 block wall meets it. Order is now: frame, then thicker, then longer, then alphabetical.
corner_ownership_2026_09_04.why_the_correction_is_certain: It reproduces every figure the owner had computed independently, where "thicker wins" reproduced none: R2 = 1675 clear + 250 = 1925 (his arithmetic, verbatim); R8 = 1490 + 300 = 1790 and R9 the same (the figure he "remembered"). His numbers chose the rule.
corner_ownership_2026_09_04.and_it_settles_the_1925_argument: !! R2 = 1925 is the exact number the owner corrected me on two rounds earlier. Both of us were right: 1675 is the CLEAR run and 1925 is the SOLID. They are different quantities and the model now carries both, so neither has to win. My error was never the 1925 - it was calling it the internal dimension.
corner_ownership_2026_09_04.the_eight_corners: R1a +250 · R1b +120 · R2 +250 · R4 +75 · R5 +75 · R8 +300 +300 · R9 +300. Every owner is a concrete frame member, which is the rule showing its work. Every other wall: solid_mm = clear_mm.
corner_ownership_2026_09_04.v19_still_DREW_the_void: ⚠ The owner had to raise the same objection twice. v19 put the ownership in the ledger and in the labels but left the DRAWING showing clear runs - so R1a still stopped at R1b’s face while MC ran through R7, two corners drawn two ways in one drawing. His test, "compare R1a|R1b with R7|MC", is exactly right. Fixed in v21: all owners drawn through, and the other wall trimmed to their face.
corner_ownership_2026_09_04.a_thin_partition_is_a_BUTT_not_a_corner: !! Rule 0, added 2026-09-04. A partition of 120 mm or less meeting a concrete frame member forms a BUTT, never a corner: it lands on the column’s face and the column does not wrap around it, so neither length changes. The owner’s wording, about R4 and R5: "the length is clear, it is 1050, and that’s it - there is no hidden section, so no solid part." Encoding it as a rule rather than an exception drops R4, R5 AND R1b - leaving exactly the owners he named (R2, R8, R9) plus R1a, which he had asked to extend two rounds earlier. R1b he did not mention, but it is the same case as R4. Five corners now, down from ten.
corner_ownership_2026_09_04.the_five_corners: R1a +250 · R2 +250 · R8 +300 +300 · R9 +300. Every owner is a concrete frame member. Solid is now shown only where a hidden section really exists.

collinear_successors_2026_09_04.finding: !! A sweep for collinear runs found ELEVEN places where one wall LINE changes thickness rather than ending. Four of them are a 250 concrete column continuing as a 75 partition: R4→G8, R5→G7, R8→G8, R9→G7.
collinear_successors_2026_09_04.this_is_where_the_printed_175_comes_from: 250 - 75 = 175 is the column PROJECTING past the partition that continues its own line. The plan prints 175 next to R4, R5, R7 and R9 - exactly these four. The owner had said this from the start ("we have thicker concrete columns and thinner dividers... this is my guess"); all I could do earlier was say where it was NOT. It is now located.
collinear_successors_2026_09_04.why_it_had_to_be_modelled: Treating successors as independent walls INVENTS junctions that do not exist. A wall crossing that line meets it once, at the dominant member - the frame, then the thickest. Before this was modelled, the checker reported a corner between G4d and G8 when the element G4d actually meets there is R4, and a corner between G4a and G4b when the west-wall line’s member at that height is R1b. Both were phantom corners that would have added material twice.

shafts_and_plumbing_to_standard_2026_09_.RETRACTION_V1_was_never_1140x490: !! I had V1 as 1140 × 490. shafts_and_plumbing_to_standard_2026_09_.but_the_1140_is_the_wrong_floor: ⚠ 1140 × 400 is the DETAILED plan’s block - two big plus two small voids, floors 10 and up. shafts_and_plumbing_to_standard_2026_09_.P2_defines_the_gap_it_sits_in: P2 is 400 wide, matching the shaft standard, and 200 deep - and the clearance from R3 to V2 IS 200. So P2 does not float in that gap, it defines it. I had measured 450 × 225; the owner’s figures are exact.

shafts_and_plumbing_to_standard_2026_09_.V1_on_the_4th_floor_RESOLVED: !! The owner: V1 has ONE section on his floor, not two, so its length is "similar to V2". That is arithmetically exact - 1140 (the detailed plan, floors 10 and up) minus the 455 mm section his floor does not have gives 685, which is V2’s length EXACTLY. shafts_and_plumbing_to_standard_2026_09_.V1_footprint_flag_CLEARED: V1’s footprint had been flagged for four rounds because my reading implied 0.315 m2 where 0.18 was expected. shafts_and_plumbing_to_standard_2026_09_.V1_measured_off_the_BASIC_plan: V1 = 700 × 400, set 150 mm clear of R1b’s inner face and against R1a. variance_against_real_flats_2026_09_04.source: 00_Master/Geometry_Variance_Study.md - the owner’s readings of floor plan_1/_2/_3, surveys of REAL completed flats of this layout, against the developer’s drawing. The first time this model has been tested against anything built.
variance_against_real_flats_2026_09_04.the_big_room_closes_three_ways: !! R2 1675 + G5 4035 + R7 1750 = 7460, and floor plan_1 measures 7460 EXACTLY while floor plan_3 measures 7450. The developer’s printed chain, one real survey and a second real survey all agree. The big room’s east side is settled.
variance_against_real_flats_2026_09_04.RETIRED_the_real_is_usually_bigger_assum: !! The owner said early on that "usually it is a little bit bigger, the real dimension". This data does not support it. The divider comes out BIGGER in reality (+20, +30), both room widths come out SMALLER (−15 to −45), and the long axis is dead on (0, −10). Deviation is roughly symmetric and depends on which dimension, not on a direction of bias - so nothing can be pre-compensated, and anything cut to a dimension must be measured on site.
variance_against_real_flats_2026_09_04.the_middle_room_window_wall: !! MB: the developer chain is 1800 + 600 + 600 = 3000, every term round; both real flats measure 2970. Two independent surveys landing on the SAME 30 mm shortfall is not noise - 3000 reads as a nominal chain and 2970 as the built result. MB carries O2, so MEASURE MB BEFORE ORDERING ANYTHING FOR THAT WINDOW.
variance_against_real_flats_2026_09_04.tolerance_now_measured: The repo carried "dimensions nominal ±25 mm" with no evidence. Observed spread reaches 45 mm, so it is now ±50 mm and measured rather than assumed. That is the BUILD tolerance; the raster tolerance in tools/layout/check_wall_junctions.py stays 25 mm and is a different quantity.
variance_against_real_flats_2026_09_04.what_the_real_plans_may_NOT_be_used_for: ⚠ They are DIFFERENT flats, possibly mirrored. They BOUND the error; they do not refine a number. Never average a developer figure with a measured one, and never use a survey of another flat to settle a dimension this flat’s drawing leaves open - R1a, the R3|G3 split.

room_rollouts_a_second_model_2026_09_04.owner_question: "The length of a wall section lets us construct the framework. But a slightly different question is the inner walls - for each room we need the rollout of all of the walls, to calculate the total area, to design the wall in different parts. Walls with the thickness is good for building the framework, but we need also internal dimensions. How are we gonna store the data per room?"
room_rollouts_a_second_model_2026_09_04.answer_two_models_not_one: !! data/canonical/room_rollouts.csv, one row per internal FACE in walk order around a room, alongside wall_blocks.csv, one row per WALL. Conflating the two is what made the earlier room-face schedule unusable and is why he told me to go back to the wall blocks. wall_blocks answers "what is built and how much of it"; room_rollouts answers "what does a person standing in this room see, and what must be finished".
room_rollouts_a_second_model_2026_09_04.why_a_face_is_not_a_wall: One wall gives a face to two rooms at two different lengths. A ventilation shaft and a plumbing block give faces but are not walls. And a STEP - the 175 mm where a 250 concrete column projects past the 75 partition continuing its line - is a face with NO WALL OF ITS OWN, so it can only exist in the rollout. The owner walked the living room and named every step, which is what made the structure obvious.
room_rollouts_a_second_model_2026_09_04.schema: room_id, seq, face_id, element, kind (wall_face | step | opening | shaft_face | plumbing_face), direction, length_mm, height_mm, contains_opening, source, notes.
room_rollouts_a_second_model_2026_09_04.the_closure_test: !! Going round a room the eastward lengths must equal the westward, and the northward the southward. A rollout that does not close has a missing or mismeasured face, and the first thing to look for is a STEP. Enforced by tools/layout/check_room_rollout.py at the ±50 mm build tolerance.
room_rollouts_a_second_model_2026_09_04.first_room_and_it_closes_exactly_on_one_: !! The кухня+living space, from the owner’s own walk. North-south: R9 820 + G7 3250 + R5 1050 + O10 1455 + V2 685 + P2 200 = 7460 EXACTLY, the figure he called the longest wall in the flat. Six segments, five of them his, summing with no residual at all. And it is a SECOND independent confirmation of O10 = 1455: with my earlier measured 1410 the sum would be 7415, 45 short.
room_rollouts_a_second_model_2026_09_04.the_open_axis: ⚠ East-west leaves −220 mm: MC 3315 + two 175 steps = 3665 going west against a 3445 pixel read of the space’s north face going east. Two causes are likely and both are in his own words - he stopped at "then the whole way and so on", so his walk did not reach the G3|R2 and MC|R7 ends, where one or two more STEPS should be; and KL-01 crosses the undimensioned R3|G3 split, so it is the least trustworthy face in the room.
room_rollouts_a_second_model_2026_09_04.areas_here_are_derived: The 51.44 m2 of finishable face is computed from linear dimensions × the 2500 mm clear height. It is never typed in and never read off a plan - the areas rule holds.

photo_evidence_brief_2026_09_04.owner_offer: Photos of other completed flats of this layout, with an annotated general plan marking each camera position and view direction.
photo_evidence_brief_2026_09_04.answer: Yes to the orientation map, and the map is worth more than the photos. Mis-assignment is the dominant error class in this model - four figures retracted in two days (G3 = 3315, G4b = 1140, the 1795, V1’s 490) and every one was a real number attached to the wrong element. A photo without a known viewpoint is another chance to make exactly that mistake.
photo_evidence_brief_2026_09_04.the_governing_distinction: !! These are photos of OTHER flats. They are STRONG evidence for building-wide standards (sill and head heights, vent outlet type, pipe stub arrangement, radiator provision, glazing spec) and for what EXISTS at all, because those do not vary flat to flat. They are WEAK for this flat’s dimensions - per Geometry_Variance_Study.md another flat bounds the error at −45 to +30 mm and never refines this flat’s number. So the camera should be aimed at standards and existence, not at dimensions.
photo_evidence_brief_2026_09_04.how_a_photo_becomes_a_measurement: A photo carries no scale unless something of KNOWN length is in frame; then everything in that plane is measurable by ratio. The model already knows: O2 and O3 openings 1800 wide, the туалет wall 1140, V1 700 × 400, the ванная 1800 deep, the 9.36 room 1795, concrete 250, partition 75, the step 175. Shoot square-on to the wall.
photo_evidence_brief_2026_09_04.highest_value_shot: !! The window wall square-on with the whole 1800 opening in frame, in BOTH the middle room and the living room. It settles the sill and head heights for O2 and O3 - the largest gap left in the model - and since those are a building standard another flat’s window answers it for this one. Everything about the window bands is currently blocked on it: plaster area, radiator space below, curtain fixing above, glazing cost. Both rooms are needed because the owner has said O3’s sill is lower and its opening taller.

soundproofing_applied_analysis_2026_09_0.question: The owner: "probably the only room which really needs soundproofing is the smaller bedroom - but to make sure, we can analyse this one more time."
soundproofing_applied_analysis_2026_09_0.answer: His instinct is half right, and the wrong half matters more. The small bedroom does carry the flat’s one bad NEIGHBOUR adjacency, but the wall involved is 250 mm reinforced concrete - the best kind this flat has. The genuinely weak walls are the internal 75 mm partitions, which no norm forces up and which separate our own bedrooms from each other.
soundproofing_applied_analysis_2026_09_0.the_worst_wall_is_G8: !! G8, 75 mm aerated block, between the 9.36 bedroom (the adults in Phase 1) and the middle room (the children). A third of the party wall’s thickness and a fraction of its mass, and the only wall in the flat where the noise is nightly and bidirectional. In Phase 2, when the boy takes the 9.36 room, G7 takes over the same role against the living zone.
soundproofing_applied_analysis_2026_09_0.and_the_vaults_own_sources_decide_the_OR: !! The repo already carries practitioner guidance that treating one wall against a NEIGHBOUR under-delivers, because that noise arrives through the перекрытие - "грамотная шумоизоляция - это ПОМЕЩЕНИЕ В ПОМЕЩЕНИИ". But between our OWN rooms both sides sit on the same slab and the dominant path through a 75 mm partition is direct airborne - so a single-wall treatment does most of the work there. Treat the walls whose noise is airborne and ours; do not treat the wall whose noise is structural and someone else’s.

RETRACTION_the_110_sewer_socket_2026_09_.what_I_claimed: That 9e9b showed the kitchen sewer connection as a 110 mm PVC socket on P2, centre 153 mm above the floor - and that its own diameter reading of 113 was "the check that the scale is right rather than merely plausible".

RETRACTION_the_110_sewer_socket_2026_09_.the_height_was_wrong_too_and_separately: I took the floor line 28 px too low - further out on the floor rather than at the wall junction. RETRACTION_the_110_sewer_socket_2026_09_.THE_ERROR_THAT_MATTERS_IS_CIRCULAR_VALID: !! I measured the PLASTERED BLOB around the pipe, got 126 mm, called it 113, and then wrote that "113 reads as a standard 110 socket, which is the check that the scale is right rather than merely plausible". That is circular: I used the object being measured to validate the scale that produced the measurement, and presented it as verification. A number cannot check itself. This is worse than the O3 sill error, because there I simply read the wrong edge - here I read the wrong edge and then dressed the coincidence up as a cross-check.
RETRACTION_the_110_sewer_socket_2026_09_.AND_A_FUNCTIONAL_CHECK_WOULD_HAVE_CAUGHT: !! DN110 is for a WC. A kitchen sink, dishwasher and washing machine all run DN50. There is no WC in the kitchen zone, so 110 was implausible before a single pixel was measured. The owner saw that immediately. THE RULE: before measuring what something is, ask what it could plausibly be. A dimension that contradicts function is wrong even when the pixels agree.
RETRACTION_the_110_sewer_socket_2026_09_.what_the_object_actually_is: ⚠ UNRESOLVED, and recorded as SP-K rather than named. O9_glazing_width_CONFIRMED_by_measuremen.the_owners_observation: Apartment 53’s plan prints 2.93 m for the лоджия glazing width. He asks whether to adopt it, and whether ours could differ.
O9_glazing_width_CONFIRMED_by_measuremen.the_agreement: !! Our derived figure is 2939 - hypot of MA’s 2825 and the 810 mm splay. His measurement is 2930. NINE MILLIMETRES apart, 0.3%. That is the best agreement any figure in this model has achieved against an independent measurement: better than the west edge (36 mm), better than G4C (34 mm), better than the big room’s long axis (10 and 20 mm).
O9_glazing_width_CONFIRMED_by_measuremen.and_it_validates_the_SPECULATIVE_part: !! The 2939 was never measured. It was DERIVED from an inconsistency - M2 at 1850 could not match M6b + R8 at 2660 if the лоджия were rectangular - and that is what produced the trapezoid finding and finally explained why the plan draws O9 as a DIAGONAL, something the drawing had been telling me for six versions. A measured 2930 confirms the whole chain, not just the number at the end of it.
O9_glazing_width_CONFIRMED_by_measuremen.does_it_matter_practically: No. 2939 gives 7.35 m² of glazing at the 2500 clear height and 2930 gives 7.33 - a 0.3% difference, inside the ±50 mm build tolerance by a factor of five, and far inside what a glazier will re-measure on site before cutting anything. Glazing is a cut-to-size item, so the model’s job here is cost estimation and confirming geometry, and both figures do that identically.
O9_glazing_width_CONFIRMED_by_measuremen.so_which_to_keep: Keep 2939 as OURS, and record 2930 as independent corroboration rather than overwriting with it. Our figure comes from our own flat’s dimensions; his comes from a different flat. Per the standing limit in Geometry_Variance_Study.md, another flat’s survey BOUNDS the error and does not refine the number - and here it bounds it at 9 mm, which is the strongest form that limit can take.
O9_glazing_width_CONFIRMED_by_measuremen.could_ours_differ: Apartment 53’s лоджия is 5.9 m² full against our 6.05, so ours is ~2.5% larger. If that difference sat in the WIDTH, ours would be ~3004 rather than 2930. But the two width figures agree to 9 mm, so the area difference must sit in the DEPTH or in how the area was computed - meaning the GLAZING WIDTH IS COMMON to both flats and the 2.5% is elsewhere. That is a useful conclusion in its own right: it is the one лоджия dimension that can be treated as a building standard.

ceiling_height_TESTED_2026_09_07.question: The owner: "Can we verify the ceiling height? I am still not sure if it is 2500 or closer to 2550."
ceiling_height_TESTED_2026_09_07.first_the_honest_limit: A direct photo measurement CANNOT settle this. The question is a 2% difference and my edge-placing error is 3-7% - demonstrated on this very question: bc18 gives anywhere from 2500 to 2676 depending on a single 25 px call on a plaster edge. Any method that reads the ceiling off a photo and compares it to 2500 is also circular, because 2500 was the scale.
ceiling_height_TESTED_2026_09_07.ROUTE_A_a_manufactured_door_standard: a82a’s far wall is FRONTAL and shows BOTH the doorway heads AND the ceiling, so a RATIO can be taken with no scale at all: head-to-ceiling / floor-to-head = 58/257 = 0.2257, hence ceiling = door head × 1.2257. A standard interior door block needs a ~2071 opening, which gives 2538. At 2050 it gives 2513; at 2100, 2574.
ceiling_height_TESTED_2026_09_07.ROUTE_B_the_owners_own_tape: living_room_window, scaled by the TAPE-measured O3 opening height of 1985 mm over 360 px = 5.514 mm/px. Head-to-ceiling measures 52 px = 287 mm, and O3’s head is 266 + 1985 = 2251 by tape. So ceiling = 2251 + 287 = 2538.
ceiling_height_TESTED_2026_09_07.THE_RESULT: !! Two independent routes - one using a manufactured door standard, one using his own tape measurements - both give ~2538. NEITHER assumes a ceiling height. ±60 mm, so 2480-2600, centred well above 2500. THE EVIDENCE LEANS HIS WAY: ~2540 rather than 2500.
ceiling_height_TESTED_2026_09_07.how_that_reconciles_with_the_developer: The developer states "высота потолков в квартирах 2,5 метра". In Russian usage высота потолков is the CLEAR height, not slab-to-slab, which would be высота этажа - and quoting a separate 3 m for the 21st floor shows they mean the usable room height, since that is what a buyer cares about. So 2,5 м reads as a NOMINAL figure and ~2540 as what was built. Builders quoting 2.5 and delivering 2.52-2.55 is ordinary.
ceiling_height_TESTED_2026_09_07.AND_THE_RISK_HE_HAS_NOT_CONSIDERED_RUNS_: ⚠ He is worried it might be MORE than 2500. The likelier error is LESS. If the developer’s 2500 is a pre-screed structural figure, then after the 50-80 mm screed the flats show in every photo the clear height would be 2420-2450. The two routes above argue against that - they measure the screeded condition and give 2538 - but it is the direction worth being alert to, because it is the one that costs money.
ceiling_height_TESTED_2026_09_07.what_to_do: Keep 2500 as the working DATUM and record ~2540 as the derived estimate. 2500 is the developer’s stated figure and the CONSERVATIVE one for clearances; 2540 is the better one for quantities. Where the two differ materially, use the safe direction rather than the best guess.
ceiling_height_TESTED_2026_09_07.where_the_40_mm_actually_matters: Finish area: +1.6%, about 3 m² over ~200 m² of wall - marginal. HEADROOM: a 2500-tall wardrobe does not fit under 2500 but does under 2540 - a buying decision, not a rounding. DROPPED CEILING: 40 mm more to give away over the кухня zone, where the vent grille at ~2.2 m already forces a duct run across. And O3’s head band becomes 289 rather than 249, which changes curtain fixing.
ceiling_height_TESTED_2026_09_07.the_one_photo_that_would_settle_it: A SQUARE-ON shot of a window wall including the ceiling. 9902 is square-on but crops the ceiling out; living_room_window includes the ceiling but is oblique. One frame with both, and the tape-measured 1985 opening height gives the ceiling to ±20 mm.

services_plan_v1_2026_09_07.CONFIDENCE_IS_DRAWN_not_just_written: !! Three symbols, because the difference matters more here than anywhere else in the model. device_counts_per_wall_form_2026_09_07.and_why_a_count_is_ENOUGH_not_a_compromi: !! A count does not give the position ALONG the wall - and that is the least important thing here. He is rewiring completely, so existing positions are reference only; ±150 mm along a wall changes no decision; and anything cut or drilled gets set out on site. device_counts_per_wall_form_2026_09_07.the_structural_point: !! That inverts the current arrangement, where the drawing is the source and the count is a description of it - which is how four sockets appeared on a party wall that should carry fewer.
